Q8007.label: Franklin Delano Roosevelt
Q8007.desc: president of the United States from 1933 to 1945 (1882–1945)
Q8007.summary: Franklin Delano Roosevelt, also known as FDR, was the 32nd president of the United States, serving from 1933 until his death in 1945. He is the longest-serving US president and the only one to have served more than two terms. His first two terms centered on combating the Great Depression, while his third and fourth focused on US involvement in World War II. A member of the Democratic Party, Roosevelt served in the New York State Senate from 1911 to 1913 and as the 44th governor of New York from 1929 to 1932.

Positions held: member of the State Senate of New York

Q887623.label: Julio Adalberto Rivera Carballo
Q887623.summary: Julio Adalberto Rivera Carballo was a Salvadoran politician and military officer, who was the 34th President of El Salvador, in office from 1962 to 1967.

Q3911.label: Albert II of Belgium
Q3911.summary: Albert II is a member of the Belgian royal family who reigned as King of the Belgians from 1993 until his abdication in 2013.

Q156487.summary: Péter Medgyessy is a retired Hungarian politician who served as Prime Minister of Hungary from 27 May 2002 to 29 September 2004.

Q4709191.label: Albanian constitutional referendum, 1994
Q4709191.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Albania on 7 November 1994. Voters were asked whether they approved of the new constitution published on 6 October, which would have given more power to the country's president. However, it was rejected by voters, with just 43.6% in favour. Voter turnout was 84.4%.

Q1087815.label: 2008 Serbian presidential election
Q1087815.summary: Presidential elections were held in Serbia on January 20 and February 3, 2008. Incumbent President Boris Tadić was re-elected as president in the second round with 51% of the vote, defeating challenger Tomislav Nikolić.

Q3544903.label: Freethinkers' Party
Q3544903.desc: Greek nationalist and monarchist political party
Q3544903.summary: The Freethinkers' Party or Free Opinion Party was a Greek nationalist and monarchist party founded and led by Ioannis Metaxas who was the Prime Minister and dictator of Greece from 1936 to 1941. It was formally founded in November 1922 after the adoption of the party's manifesto that was unveiled on 13 October 1922. Metaxas had the party and all other parties dissolved following the establishment of the 4th of August Regime, in which he ruled as an official independent.

Q13479751.label: 1945 Bulgarian parliamentary election
Q13479751.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Bulgaria on 18 November 1945, the country's first to feature universal suffrage for women. The Bulgarian Agrarian National Union and the Bulgarian Communist Party both won 94 seats. Voter turnout was 84.8%.

Q1993031.label: 2006 Bulgarian presidential election
Q1993031.summary: Presidential elections were held in Bulgaria on 22 October 2006, as decided on 27 July 2006 by the Bulgarian Parliament. The runoff took place on 29 October 2006, while the electoral campaign spanned 19 September – 20 October. At the election, Georgi Parvanov won his second and final term as President of Bulgaria.

Q131152711.label: 2024 Zhuhai car attack
Q131152711.img: Zhuhai Stadium west gate after 2024 Zhuhai car attack - Nov.12,2024.jpg
Q131152711.summary: On 11 November 2024, 62-year-old Fan Weiqiu drove his SUV into people on the exercise track at the Zhuhai Stadium sports center in Zhuhai, Guangdong, China, killing 38 and injuring 48 more. Weiqiu then attempted to kill himself with a knife; he was taken into custody and sent to a hospital.

mentions.c: People's Republic of China: Terrorist attack: 2024 Zhuhai car attack

Q717127.label: Seven Enemy Offensives
Q717127.desc: Periodization of the World War II in Yugoslavia.
Q717127.img: Long live the Yugoslav National Army, the protector of freedom of our people, Yugoslavia 1945.png
Q717127.summary: The Seven Enemy Offensives is a group name used in Yugoslav historiography to refer to seven major Axis military operations undertaken during World War II in Yugoslavia against the Yugoslav Partisans.

Q208199.label: Sabra and Shatila massacre
Q208199.desc: the killing of between 460 and 3,500 Christians, mostly Arab Palestinians in Beirut, Lebanon; during the1982 Lebanon War
Q208199.img: Dead bodies piled up in Shatila camp, Beirut, Lebanon, on 20 September 1982. Several hundred Palestine refugees and other civilians were massacred in the Sabra and Shatila districts of south Beirut between 16 and 18 September.jpg
Q208199.summary: From 16 to 18 September 1982, between 1,300 and 3,500 civilians—mostly Palestinians and Lebanese Shias—were killed in Beirut's Sabra neighbourhood and the adjacent Shatila refugee camp by the Lebanese Forces, one of the main Christian militias in Lebanon, with the support of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF).

mentions.c: Part of Lebanese Civil War; 700 deaths

Q4202311.label: Iraqi attack on USS Stark
Q4202311.desc: military incident between the United States and Iraq
Q4202311.img: USS Stark (FFG-31) listing after missile hit in the Persian Gulf on 18 May 1987.jpeg
Q4202311.summary: The USS Stark incident occurred during the Iran–Iraq War in the Persian Gulf on 17 May 1987, when an Iraqi jet aircraft fired two Exocet missiles at the U.S. frigate USS Stark. A total of 37 United States Navy personnel were killed or later died as a result of the attack, and 21 were injured. Iraq apologized, and Saddam Hussein said that the pilot mistook the frigate for an Iranian tanker.

Q124255559.label: Iraqi rocket attacks on Saudi Arabia
Q124255559.desc: 1991 Iraqi military operations targeting American bases
Q124255559.summary: Between 18 January and 26 February 1991, Iraq launched 46 al-Husayn Scud missiles against Saudi Arabian and American military targets in Dhahran and the Saudi capital of Riyadh amidst the Gulf War. Attacks began hours after US General Norman Schwarzkopf emphasized large-scale efforts taken to comb the vast expanses of western Iraq for missile attacks aimed at Israel.

Q30589255.label: Operation Hammer Down
Q30589255.summary: Operation Hammer Down was a seven-day U.S.-led assault offensive in June 2011 designed to eliminate foreign fighters and training camps in the Watapur Valley of Kunar Province in Afghanistan in preparation of an eventual push into the Western Pech area. The operation's primary objective was to destroy suspected training camps at the northern end of the Watapur in order to interdict the flow of insurgents through the valley and forbid the Taliban from increasing their manpower in the western Pech.

Q291143.label: Linda Sánchez
Q291143.summary: Linda Teresa Sánchez is an American politician and former labor lawyer serving as the U.S. representative for California's 38th congressional district since 2013. A member of the Democratic Party, she was first elected to Congress in 2002 in California's 39th congressional district. Sánchez serves on the Ways and Means Committee; she was the ranking member on the House Ethics Committee until 2017. In the 114th Congress, she chaired the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

Positions held: Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman of the United States House of Representatives

Q11079.label: Al-Battani
Q11079.summary: Al-Battani, archaically Latinized as Albategnius, was an Arab Muslim astronomer, astrologer, geographer and mathematician, who lived and worked for most of his life at Raqqa, now in Syria. He is considered to be one of the greatest and most famous of the astronomers of the medieval Islamic world.

mentions.c: Al-Battani measures the solar year (c. AD 900)

Q201543.label: Niccolò Tartaglia
Q201543.img: Portret van Niccolo Tartaglia Nicolavs Tartaglia Brixianvs (titel op object) Portretten van beroemde Europese geleerden (serietitel) Virorum doctorum de Disciplinis benemerentium effigies (serietitel), RP-P-1909-4459.jpg
Q201543.summary: Nicolo, known as Tartaglia, was an Italian mathematician, engineer, a surveyor and a bookkeeper from the then Republic of Venice. He published many books, including the first Italian translations of Archimedes and Euclid, and an acclaimed compilation of mathematics. Tartaglia was the first to apply mathematics to the investigation of the paths of cannonballs, known as ballistics, in his Nova Scientia ; his work was later partially validated and partially superseded by Galileo's studies on falling bodies. He also published a treatise on retrieving sunken ships.

Member of: Guglielmo da Fontaneto & Pietro Facolo & Niccolò Tartaglia

Q192839.label: Sébastien Le Prestre de Vauban
Q192839.wiki: Sébastien Le Prestre, Marquis of Vauban
Q192839.summary: Sébastien Le Prestre, Marquis of Vauban was a French Royal Army officer who served under Louis XIV. One of the most important military engineers in European history, his defensive principles remained in use for nearly 100 years after his death, while aspects of his offensive tactics were employed into the 20th century.

Q4868935.summary: The Bath Philharmonia is an orchestra based in Bath. They collaborated with Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey on the 2024 Christmas charity single "Love is Enough".

Q4920135.summary: Tesla Electric Light and Manufacturing Company was an electric lighting company in Rahway, New Jersey that operated from December 1884 through 1886.

Q381255.label: American nationalism
Q381255.desc: nationalism in support of the collective identity of the United States
Q381255.summary: American nationalism is a form of nationalism in the United States that, as a movement or ideology, views Americans as a nation that should be congruent with and represented by the government of the United States, and it supports what it perceives to be the interests of that nation. It can be subject to civic, cultural, or economic influences. Essentially, it indicates the aspects that characterize and distinguish the United States as an autonomous political community.

Q190279.label: Milesian school
Q190279.summary: The Ionian school of pre-Socratic philosophy refers to Ancient Greek philosophers, or a school of thought, in Ionia in the 6th century BC, the first in the Western tradition.

Q745799.label: Islamic Golden Age
Q745799.desc: period of cultural flourishing in the 8th to 13th centuries
aliases: history of the Islamic Golden Age (750-1258)
Q745799.summary: The Islamic Golden Age was a period of cultural flourishing in the history of Islam, dated from the 8th century CE to the 14th century. The period is understood to have begun during the reign of the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid (786–809), with the establishment of the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, one of the world's largest cities at the time. The institution attracted scholars from across the Muslim world to translate the classical knowledge of the known world into Arabic.
